season.evidence: Logged ascents peak June (46) but skewed by courses and skiers; searches say May to mid-Oct with Jul and early Aug prime, crevasses open by late Aug. Stored Jun-Sep kept. All harvested reports are June.

track.why: Logged Easton Glacier, 9 Jun 2024; report starts from Sandy Camp, no open crevasses, snow ridge to the summit. Track starts 61 m from our Park Butte pin, passes 55 m from Sandy Camp pin, 26 m from our summit pin; ends at camp.

otherTracksConsidered.why: Jun 2025 Strava, complete round trip passing Sandy Camp (92 m) and the summit, but also goes to Grant Peak and no route is named
Squak Glacier line via Crag View camp

facts.text: In late June the Park Butte trail is snow-free low down; snow begins at the top of the switchbacks and camps near 5,400 ft are often full, so many go on to about 6,000 ft.
In late June the Easton Glacier was fully covered, roping up from camp and putting on crampons near 6,600 ft.
Late June: only one snow bridge on the Easton line looked unlikely to last a few more weeks.
Early-afternoon June descents sink thigh-deep in warm soft snow; start the return from the summit early.
The Roman Wall switchbacks are well kicked in by June; many descend them directly before the side trip to Sherman.

season.evidence: Stored Jun-Aug; searches (Mountaineers route page, summit guides, USFS ranger note) say prime July/early Aug but the bergschrund and melt-out close the line in late season; a late-season attempt failed for melt-out. Both harvested reports are June.

track.why: 8 Jun 2025 Mountaineers climb; report says they joined the Squak Glacier route at about 4,700 ft, camped at 6,100 ft near our Crag View pin, reached the saddle west of Sherman (9,800 ft) and summited. Track starts 87 m from our Park Butte pin, ends 128 m, passes 13 m from Crag View and 0 m from our summit pin.

otherTracksConsidered.why: Logged Squak, 29 Jun 2025, summit-day track from Crag View only (not complete)

facts.text: In early June the Scott Paul trail is the usual way up to about 4,700 ft before joining the glacier line; camp at Crag View is near 6,100 ft.
Early June: a deep moat splits the rock slope from the glacier just beyond camp, forcing a drop east before the climb.
A long transverse crevasse crosses the route near 7,900 ft; keep it to the right on the way up the glacier toward the saddle.
Firm crisp snow at 1-2 am in June lets you rope up at the rock edge and put on crampons a few hundred feet higher.
The final ridge from the saddle is short; one 10-ft exposed section gets pickets for running belays when partly melted out.
The loose gully at the dirty col clogs crampons with sticky volcanic mud on the way back.

notes: Crater Rim route already has 241 track points stored; 2718103 is a candidate, one-way. Peakbagger summit is 0-30 m from our pin; no move needed.
